monthly_review.summary: You've shifted toward higher-intensity running this month, with a notable increase in Zone 4 time and faster average pace, but at the cost of reduced volume and lower aerobic TE — suggesting a recent emphasis on quality over quantity.
monthly_review.highlight: Zone 4 time jumped from 15% last month to 35% this month — the largest proportional shift across all HR zones.

goal_tracker.message: You need 39.6 more km across 7 remaining sessions — averaging ~5.7 km per run — to match last month’s volume. Given your recent 10.0 km long run and strong aerobic TE (4.0), 3–4 runs of 6–8 km at Zone 2–3 HR would be realistic and sustainable.

insights.title: Improved efficiency despite higher intensity
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency rose from 13.46 to 13.9 km/hr per bpm this month, even as avg HR increased +5 bpm and Zone 4 time tripled — indicating better cardiovascular economy under load.

insights.title: Zone 4 dominance displaces foundational Zone 2 time
insights.body: Zone 4 now accounts for 35% of total HR time (up from 15%), while Zone 2 dropped from 29% to 15% — reducing time spent building aerobic base and recovery capacity.

insights.title: Cadence decline correlates with longer efforts and fatigue
insights.body: Avg cadence fell from 151 spm (June) to 148 spm (July), and the slowest cadence (136 spm) occurred on the 4.0 km recovery run (7/08) — suggesting form breakdown at low HR, possibly due to accumulated fatigue or insufficient recovery.

insights.title: High-intensity density without compensatory recovery
insights.body: Three of your last five runs (6.5 km, 10.0 km, 4.0 km) were completed in just 4 days (7/01–7/08), with only one true easy day (0.9 km on 7/06); yet VO2 max remains stable at 39.0 — a sign resilience is holding, but not indefinitely.

recommendations.action: Do your next run as a strict 6.0 km Zone 2 session (HR ≤135 bpm), focusing on cadence ≥150 spm and stride length ≥75 cm.
recommendations.reason: To rebuild Zone 2 volume (down 14% MoM) and counter cadence drift observed in recent easy efforts.

recommendations.action: Insert a full rest day before your next long run — no activity except walking — following the 10.0 km effort on 7/05.
recommendations.reason: Your 7/08 run showed lowest cadence (136 spm) and lowest HR (129 bpm), signaling residual fatigue; Garmin VO2 max has plateaued at 39.0, indicating no recent aerobic gain without recovery.

recommendations.action: Perform a 5-minute cadence drill post-run: 1 min @ 155 spm, 1 min @ 160 spm, 1 min @ 155 spm, 2 min @ 152 spm — immediately after your next two Zone 2 runs.
recommendations.reason: To reinforce neuromuscular patterning and offset the -3 spm MoM cadence drop, especially since ground contact time improved slightly (312 → 300 ms) but cadence declined.

weekly_focus.description: Re-establish Zone 2 endurance capacity and neuromuscular coordination lost during recent high-Zone 4 emphasis — prioritizing consistency, rhythm, and recovery responsiveness over pace or distance targets.
suggested_sessions: 6 km Zone 2 run (HR ≤135 bpm, cadence ≥150 spm)
45-min easy walk or mobility session (zero HR data required)
3 km progressive run: 1 km Z2 → 1 km Z3 → 1 km Z2, focusing on smooth transitions
